caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 93 of 2002
lawyer:
Md Abdus Sobhan, Senior Advocate instructed by Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Respondents—Not represented.
parties:
Md Dulal ------ Petitioner
Vs.
State and another ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
MM Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 20-5-2002 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1937 of 2000, registered upon an application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, discharging the Rule. 

 2. The respondent No. 2 filed Miscellaneous Petition No. 3180 of 1996 before the Thana Magistrate, Bamna on 28-12-1996 on the allegations, inter alia, that on 24-12-1996 at 11-00 hours when she went to paddy field of her husband, the convict-petitioner came to her and gave proposal for co-habitation but she refused. At this the convict-petitioner forcibly raped her causing injury on her breast and had torn her blouse. She could not raise hue and cry as the accused petitioner pushed his shirt into her mouth. 

 3. Police after investigating the case submitted final report. The learned Magistrate then sent the case record to the learned Judge of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat, Barguna. The learned Public Prosecution filed an application before the Bishesh Adalat for taking cognizance under section 6(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 1995 against the accused-petitioner only. 

 6. Convict-petitioner then preferred Miscellaneous Case No.1937 of 2000 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the order of conviction and sentence before the High Court Division and by the impugned judgment the High Court Division discharged the Rule. 

 7. We have heard Mr Md Abdus Sobhan, the learned Counsel for the petitioner. lie mainly argued that since in this case police after investigation submitted final report with a prayer for prosecuting the informant of the case under section 211 of the Penal Code taking cognizance of the case because of the provision of section 17 of the Act by the learned Judge of Bishesh Adalat was illegal and this vitiated the whole trial and consequently, the order of conviction and sentence of the petitioner has also been vitiated. Therefore, the High Court Division was not justified in discharging the Rule. 

 9. In the instant case the Court on perusal of the police report was satisfied that there were materials for taking cognizance against the petitioner under section 6(1) of the Ain and thereupon took cognizance.
